title: THE GOD PARTICLE
excerpt: Imagine a world where the faster you drag yourself through space, the heavier you become.
body:
Imagine a universe filled with particles, none of which have mass. Sounds impossible, doesn't it? Our immediate reaction is to ask: How can something exist without mass? Let us try to picture such a world. Electrons, quarks, and other fundamental particles would have no mass and, if truly massless, would travel at the speed of light. The familiar atoms that make up our world could not form as they do today. No stars, no planets, and certainly no you or me as we exist now.

And this was exactly the case when the universe began. So what changed? As particle physics advanced, scientists struggled to explain why these elementary particles acquired mass later on. To resolve this gaping hole in our understanding, theoretical physicists devised an elegant mathematical concept: an invisible field that permeates all of space known as the Higgs Field. The idea was bold, but how could anyone prove that something invisible actually existed? Even Stephen Hawking famously wagered $100 against physicist Gordon Kane, betting that the Higgs particle would never be discovered.

To understand what scientists were looking for, imagine a perfectly still ocean. From a distance, its surface might appear calm and difficult to discern. Now throw a rock into it. A ripple spreads across the water, revealing movement in something that was already there. What if a similar idea could help us detect a field that we cannot see? The Higgs field is present throughout space, but scientists cannot observe it directly in the way we see ordinary objects. Instead, they searched for an excitation of the field: the Higgs boson. Just as a ripple is a disturbance in water, the Higgs boson is a disturbance in the Higgs field.

In 2012, at CERN (fascinatingly where the World Wide Web was born), scientists used the Large Hadron Collider to generate that microscopic splash. They confirmed the existence of the Higgs field, and with it, the mechanism responsible for giving fundamental particles their mass.

How does it actually work? As fundamental particles move through the Higgs field, they interact with it and the strength of that interaction dictates their mass. Particles like photons pass right through without interacting, zooming along at the speed of light proving that they are massless. Particles like quarks drag through this field and gain mass through their continuous interaction. And in a fascinating twist of nature, the Higgs boson gains its mass by interacting with its own field.

The discovery completed the Standard Model of Physics and as for Hawking? He lost his $100 bet. 

Take a moment to appreciate what this means. A field that we cannot see, touch or directly observe in the ordinary sense helps determine the properties of the fundamental particles that make up our world. But if we cannot observe the Higgs field, all while its hidden mechanics shape everything in our world, how much of reality remains hidden beneath the surface of what we can see?

As for the dramatic name everyone knows it by? The nickname "God Particle" was created by the Nobel Prize-winning physicist Leon Lederman originally wanted to title his book "The Goddamn Particle" out of frustration over how difficult it was to find, but his publisher shortened it to "The God Particle" for print and the name stuck.

title: THE SAND RECKONER
excerpt: The universe isn't infinite, our tools just weren't big enough to count it.
body:
In his treatise The Sand Reckoner, Archimedes confronts a seemingly insurmountable question: how many grains of sand would it take to fill the universe?

At a time when Greek numerical system was ill-equipped to express quantities of extraordinary magnitude, Archimedes devised a mathematical framework that extended numerical thought far beyond its conventional limits. His objective was not to find a finite number or to count the uncountable, but to refute the prevailing notion that quantities on such an immense scale were inherently inexpressible. He sought to demonstrate that even the seemingly infinite could be approached through the disciplined language of mathematics.

By estimating the universe's diameter at no more than $10^{14}$ stadia, Archimedes calculated that filling it with sand would require a quantity equivalent to approximately $8 \times 10^{63}$ grains in modern notation, a figure far below the upper limits of his newly created system, what in modern day is referred to as the place value notation.

Archimedes demonstrated that the boundaries of knowledge are often determined less by the scale of a problem and rather the limitations of the tools with which we approach it. This leaves us with the question: If the universe can be rendered intelligible through mathematics, did he construct the most powerful framework through which the human mind can comprehend it?

title: THE ENIGMA OF CONSCIOUSNESS
excerpt: What if the boundary between your mind and the universe is merely an illusion of perspective?
quote: "Consciousness is a singular of which the plural is unknown"
body:
Erwin Schrödinger’s aphorism intimates one of the most profound enigma's of existence: whether consciousness, despite its apparent multiplicity, is fundamentally one rather than a collection of separate, self-contained experiences.

If consciousness cannot be meaningfully pluralized, then the distinction between the observer and the observed, between you and I, may be far less fundamental than our subjective experience suggests. If consciousness is singular, are we truly separate beings experiencing the universe, or is it the universe experiencing itself through us?

Just as waves are the ocean’s way of expressing movement, in a similar sense our individual consciousnesses (plural) are like a ripple in the universal mind or conscious (singular). The daily impression of separate minds may simply be this single conscious reality looking back at itself through different pairs of eyes.

While this perspective remains a philosophical interpretation rather than a scientific conclusion, it compels us to reconsider our most basic assumption of existence, inviting us to see beyond the illusion of division.
